label: early original-phase step after i/c in a sequence starting s/p/u (weak, combinatorial)
explanation: Sparse, low-magnitude feature. 94% of its mass falls in the original phase, mostly at t=3-5. It never fires at t=0-1 and rarely fires in the copy phase. It is enriched when i or c came one or two steps earlier (prev_tok i is 13x), when the sequence starts with s, p or u (s is 8x), and when the current input is i, r, u, q or w. The strongest examples look like s n i [i] [r] and u x i c [i] [r]. These cues combine without a clean rule: the best conjunction reaches only about 0.23 F1 on dev, and simpler versions have high recall but precision of 1% or less. Magnitude is highest for i/r inputs right after an earlier i in sequences starting with s/u, but I did not check magnitude beyond the top examples. It does not fire on delimiter or copy steps in any systematic way.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: prev_tok=i (+5.19), phase=2 & in_tok=u (+5.16), phase=2 & out_tok=p (+5.07), prev2_tok=i (+4.89), phase=2 & out_tok=s (+4.60), orig0=s (+4.31). Lower it: phase=2 (-4.42), t=7 (-3.27), t=9 (-3.23), prev2_tok=- (-3.07).
